blocks.text: With roughly two-thirds of large companies now reported, revenue growth is running at a modest pace while operating margins have surprised to the upside. Cost control is doing most of the work: slower hiring, tighter inventory management and lower freight and energy costs than a year ago.

Management teams have largely reiterated full-year targets but widened their ranges. The word **discipline** appears with unusual frequency on earnings calls, typically referring to hiring, inventory and capital spending outside priority areas.

items: Capital-light business models are being rewarded as refinancing costs rise.
Consumer companies report a split between resilient higher-income spending and trading down elsewhere.
Industrial firms cite steady order books but longer customer decision cycles.

blocks.text: Markets are paying for evidence of durable margins rather than headline beats. With the cost of capital higher for longer, companies that can fund growth internally hold a structural advantage.
